narrative:
The model determined that you have a 35% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were your credit history, the length of the loan you requested, and the status of your checking account. Your credit history of critical or other existing credits was the strongest influence, and it pushed the prediction toward approval rather than denial. The shorter 11-month duration you asked for also worked in your favor, as it is well below the 19-month average seen among approved applicants. Unfortunately, the status of your checking account proved decisive. Having a balance between 0 and 200 DM is relatively uncommon among successful applicants and this factor alone pulled the prediction strongly toward bad credit risk, outweighing the positive signals from the other two features.

Taken together, these top influences led the model to conclude that the risk was too high to approve the loan.

You should focus on improving the status of your checking account, perhaps by maintaining a higher balance or opening a salary account, and then reapply in a few months. This single change is likely to have the biggest positive impact on future decisions. (218 words)
